column2: この五百年、手を尽くしても、食えたのは人間五人に妖怪八十匹だけだ。この調子じゃ、あと何度五百年を待てば出られるんだ！
column3: In five hundred years, try as I might, I've eaten only five humans and eighty demons. At this rate, how many more five-hundred-years must I wait to get out!

column2: たとえ本当にそうだとしても、その時になって出る方法が分からないのは同じですわ！
column3: Even if that were true, you still wouldn't know the way out when the time came!

column2: 九十九人か千匹の妖怪を食べるという噂は、おそらく悪辣な計略です。塔に閉じ込められた妖怪たちが、互いに食い合って滅びるように仕向けたものでしょう
column3: This rumor about eating ninety-nine humans or a thousand demons is most likely a vicious scheme, meant to make the demons locked in the tower devour one another until none are left.

column2: うむ…一理ある…
column3: Hmm... that makes sense...

column2: 皆さん！　人間にはこんな言葉があります。「精神一到、何事か成らざらん」と
column3: Everyone! Humans have a saying: 'Where there's a will, there's a way.'

column2: この鎖妖塔は五百年もの間、数知れぬ妖魔を閉じ込め、一匹たりとも逃がしたことがないと言われています。でも…この塔は結局、人の手で造られたものです…。ですから、方法がないはずはないと思うのです。皆さん、心を落ち着けて、よく考えましょう。皆の知恵を集めれば、きっと良い手立てが見つかります
column3: They say this Demon-Sealing Tower has imprisoned countless demons for five hundred years without a single one escaping. But... this tower was, after all, built by human hands... So I believe there must be a way. Let us all calm down and think it through. If we pool everyone's wisdom, we will surely come up with something.

column2: うむ…よし、そうしよう！
column3: Mm... All right, let's do that!

column2: 兄弟たちよ！　頭としてここに宣言する。今日より後、仲間同士で殺し合い、食い合うことは断じて許さん。背いた者は、この天鬼皇が決して容赦せんぞ！　分かったか！？
column3: Brothers! As your boss, I hereby declare: from this day on, there will be no more killing and eating among our own. Whoever disobeys, I, the Ghost Emperor, will show no mercy! Understood!?

column2: へい、兄貴！
column3: Yes, Boss!

column2: それから…ここにいる者なら誰でもいい。皆を外へ連れ出す手立てを出せた者には、この頭の座を譲ってやる！
column3: Also... anyone here, no matter who: come up with a way to get us all out, and I'll hand over my place as boss!

column2: どうした？　誰も試してみようという者はおらんのか？
column3: Well? Is no one willing to give it a try?

column2: かような深遠な問題、おぬしらの鬼の頭をいくらひねったところで、屁のひとつも出てきはせんわ！
column3: A problem this profound? You could rack those ghostly skulls of yours till they crack and still not come up with squat!

column2: 天地の理を究め、古今の謎を解きたくば、この書中の仙人に教えを請えばよいのじゃ！
column3: If you would fathom the laws of heaven and earth and solve the riddles of the ages, just come and ask me, the Immortal of the Book!

column2: 老いぼれの本の虫め！　また何をかき回しに来た
column3: You old bookworm! What are you here to stir up this time?

column2: これ！　ごろつき鬼の頭め、口を慎まんか！　わしは今や、仙～人～なのじゃぞ
column3: Hey! Mind your tongue, you ghost thug boss! I'll have you know I am now an Im-mor-tal!

column2: たかが下等な小妖怪の分際で、仙人を名乗るとは片腹痛い！　この前の仕置きでは足りなかったか？
column3: A mere lowly little demon, daring to call himself an immortal! Was the lesson I taught you last time not enough?

column2: ははは、わしのこの書中仙人という称号は、聖霊のお嬢様のご亭主が、じきじきに授けてくださったものじゃ。おぬしが認めぬわけにはいかんぞ！
column3: Ha ha! My title of Immortal of the Book was bestowed by the Holy Maiden's own husband, in his very own words. You have no choice but to accept it!

column3: Husband? ...I bestowed it?

column2: ふん、後ろ盾ができたからって偉そうに！
column3: Hmph! So you've got a patron, big deal!

column2: これ！　おぬしら、わしの話を聞くのか聞かんのか？　この鎖妖塔から逃げ出す方法はただひとつ。しかも…それを知っておるのはわしだけじゃ！
column3: Hey! Are you going to listen to me or not? There is only one way to escape this Demon-Sealing Tower, and... only I know it!

column2: 本当ですか！　先輩、早く教えてください
column3: Really! Please, Master, tell us quickly!

column2: あの老いぼれ本の虫のたわごとを信じるな。あいつはいつも、泣くに泣けず笑うに笑えん手ばかり出してくるんだ
column3: Don't believe that old bookworm's nonsense. Every time, he comes up with ideas you don't know whether to laugh or cry at.

column2: へっへっ、だがおぬしも認めざるを得まい。どれも物事を片付ける一番の近道じゃったと
column3: Heh heh. You have to admit, those were all the most direct ways to solve the problem.

column2: ふん、八年前、俺の弟分がうっかり吸妖壺に吸い込まれた時もそうだ。助け出す方法だと言ってお前が教えたのは、頭から壺にぶつかれというものだった
column3: Hmph! Like eight years ago, when one of my brothers blundered into the Demon-Sucking Jar. Your way of getting him out was to have me ram it with my head.

column2: おかげで俺が壺に吸い込まれて、八年も閉じ込められたんだぞ！
column3: And as a result I got sucked into the jar myself and was trapped for eight whole years!

column2: おぬしのその弟分は、それで助かったではないか？
column3: And wasn't that little brother of yours saved because of it?

column2: お前は明らかに俺をはめたんだ！
column3: You were plainly out to get me!

column2: お二人とも、言い争いはおやめください。書仙様に塔を出る方法がおありなら、まずは皆でお話を伺ってみましょう

column2: ははは、聖霊のお嬢様がお顔を立ててくださるなら、わしもとっておきを披露するとしよう！　まあ聞くがよい…
column3: Ha ha! Since the Holy Maiden is kind enough to give me face, this old man shall show off his treasure! Listen well...

column2: この塔は五百八十四年前、梁の武帝が天下の金剛白玉石をあまねく集め、数千人の一流の工匠を召し、二十年の歳月を費やして築いたものじゃ…。さらに数知れぬ高僧や法師を招き、塔の内外に無数の禁呪を張り巡らせた。数百年の移り変わりを経て、今は蜀山仙剣派がこの塔を引き継いでおる。理屈から言えば、この塔には入口があるのみで出口はない。しかも四方の壁は、神兵利器でも傷つけられず、雷に打たれ火に焼かれても損なわれず、仙術も魔の呪いもまるで歯が立たぬ。建物の造りそのものの弱点を突くほかに、皆が外へ出る道はないのじゃ
column3: This tower was built five hundred and eighty-four years ago, when Emperor Wu of Liang gathered adamant white jade stone from all over the land and summoned thousands of master craftsmen, who labored for twenty years... He also had countless eminent monks and mages lay innumerable sealing spells inside and outside the tower. After centuries of change, it came under the charge of the Mount Shu Immortal Sword Sect. In theory, this tower has an entrance but no exit. What is more, its walls cannot be damaged by divine weapons or keen blades, nor harmed by lightning or fire, and immortal arts and demonic spells are utterly useless. Only by striking at a weakness in its very structure can we all get out.

column2: つまり…内側からこの塔を壊す、ということですか？
column3: Meaning... we destroy the tower from within?

column2: その通り！　皆、周りにあるこの十一本の巨大な剣の柱が見えるか？
column3: Exactly! Do you all see these eleven giant sword pillars around us?

column2: わしが長年かけて観察したところによれば…ここは鎖妖塔の最下層、精鉄で鋳られたこれらの巨剣こそ、塔を支える柱なのじゃ。わしらのいるこの一本を除き、うち七本は北斗七星の磐龍陣の方位に並び、残る三本は神龍擺尾の方位に置かれておる。すなわち龍の尾を縛っておるのじゃ
column3: From my many years of observation... this is the lowest level of the Demon-Sealing Tower, and these giant swords cast of refined iron are the very pillars that hold it up. Apart from the one where we stand, seven are arrayed in the positions of the Big Dipper's Coiled Dragon Formation, and the other three stand in the position of the Divine Dragon Swings Its Tail, which is to say, they lock down the dragon's tail.

column2: そして、そばにあるこの最も大きな剣が、ちょうど龍の頭を釘付けにしておる。かくして飛龍は陸に囚われ、上は天を絶たれ、下は地を絶たれる形勢となるわけじゃ
column3: And this largest sword beside us pins the dragon's head dead in place. Thus the flying dragon is trapped on land, cut off from heaven above and from earth below.

column2: ほう、なら話は早い。この剣の柱を全部へし折ってしまえ！
column3: Oh, that's easy then. Just smash all these sword pillars!

column2: 最後まで聞かんか、ごろつき鬼の頭め！　少しは頭を使ったらどうじゃ？　柱は下から支えておるのじゃぞ。上のほうを叩き切って何になる？
column3: Let me finish, you ghost thug boss! Can't you use your brain a little? The pillars hold things up from below. What good is chopping off the top part?

column2: 貴様…！
column3: You...!

column2: この化妖水の池の下に、これらの剣の柱を支える要が必ずあるはずじゃ
column3: Beneath this pool of Demon-Dissolving Water, there must be the points that support these sword pillars.

column2: 誰かが潜って、その場所を見つけて壊しさえすれば、この塔は嫌でも崩れ落ちるわい
column3: If someone dives down, finds those spots and destroys them, this tower can't help but collapse.

column2: 冗談じゃない！　誰が行くんだ？　この化妖水は、俺たちは一滴かかっただけでもたまらんのだ。全身で潜ったりしたら、体ごときれいさっぱり溶けちまうだろうが！
column3: You must be joking! Who's going? We can't stand even a single drop of this Demon-Dissolving Water. Dive in whole and we'd be dissolved down to nothing!

column2: その通り。この塔を設計した者が塔の底に化妖水を注いだのは、妖怪が塔の底から土遁で逃げるのを防ぐため、そしてまた、これらの剣の柱を腐食から守るためでもあった。へっへっ、じゃが…まさか人間がこの最下層までたどり着こうとは、連中も夢にも思わなかったはずじゃ
column3: Exactly. Those who designed this tower filled its base with Demon-Dissolving Water to keep demons from burrowing out through the ground below, and also to protect these sword pillars from corrosion. Heh heh... But they surely never imagined that a human could make it all the way down to this lowest level.

column2: つまり…俺が行けと？
column3: You mean... I should go?

column2: 化妖水は妖怪には命取りじゃが…人間には無害なのじゃ
column3: Demon-Dissolving Water is deadly to demons... but harmless to humans.

column2: よし、李兄さん、行きましょ！
column3: All right! Brother Li, let's go!

column2: 化妖池の水面には、ひどく粘っこい油の層が浮いておる。お二人の体重では、おそらく潜るのは難しかろう
column3: A very thick layer of oil floats on the surface of the pool. At your weight, I'm afraid the two of you will find it hard to dive through.

column2: じゃが、ここの池の水はゆっくりと流れておる。排水口の近く、流れの激しいところなら油の層も薄いゆえ、潜れるはずじゃ
column3: But the water here is slowly flowing. Near an outlet, where the current is stronger, the oil layer is thinner, and you should be able to dive down.

column3: Where is it? Around here?

column2: 排水口の場所はしょっちゅう変わるでな、わしにもどこにあるかは分からん。自分で探すがよい！
column3: The outlet's position keeps changing. I don't know where it is either. Go find it yourselves!

column2: ふう…わしの話はこれで終いじゃ。あとはおぬしらに任せる。わしは書の中に戻って休むとするわい！
column3: Phew... I've said my piece. The rest is up to you. I'm going back into my book to rest!

column3: Then that's what we'll do!

column3: Brother Ghost, leave this to me. Please spread the word to everyone in the tower: when it's done, everyone gathers here. If we're getting out, we all get out together!

column2: よし、手分けして動くぞ
column3: Good. Let's split up and get to work.

column3: Listen up, everyone! Go back and gather your wives and children, and pack up whatever belongings you want to take. When you hear my call, come back and assemble here.

column2: うまくいくよう祈ってるぞ。また後でな！
column3: Good luck with everything. See you later!

column2: あたしにはあたしのやり方があるの。心配いらないよ
column3: I have my ways. No need for you to worry.

column2: それに、タダであげるわけじゃないんだからね！　あんたにも、あるものを取りに行くのを手伝ってもらうよ
column3: And I'm not giving it to you for nothing! You have to help me go get something, too.

column2: いいとも、それは当然だ
column3: Sure, that's only fair.

column2: えへへ、約束だよ。ついてきて！)
column3: Hee hee, it's a deal. Come with me!)

column2: どこへ行くんだ？
column3: Where to?

column2: この林の中に、人目につかない木のうろがあるの。その中に妖怪が隠したお宝があってね、あんたと一緒にあるものを探しに行きたいんだよ
column3: There's a hidden tree hollow in this forest, where demons have stashed their treasures. I want you to come with me and look for something.

column2: おばあちゃん、阿奴が会いに来たよ！
column3: Granny! Anu's come to see you!

column2: ほっほっほ…よしよし
column3: Ho ho ho... good girl.

column2: 阿奴や…どうしてまた李少侠と一緒におるのじゃ？
column3: Anu... how do you come to be with young hero Li?

column2: あれ？　おばあちゃん、とっくに知り合いだったんだ！　あたし、紹介してあげようと思ってたのに
column3: Oh? You already know him, Granny! And here I was going to introduce him to you.

column2: この人ったらね、すっごく恥知らずなんだよ…。鳳凰の卵を盗もうとしただけじゃなくて、あたしにいやらしいことまでしようとしたんだから！　おばあちゃん、ひどい人だと思わない？
column3: This man, he's absolutely shameless... Not only did he try to steal the phoenix egg, he tried to take liberties with me too! Granny, isn't he just awful?

column2: ほっほっ、鳳凰の卵は、わしが取りに行かせたのじゃよ。それよりお前という子は、また母上の言いつけを聞かんで。おとなしく城で安楽に暮らしておればよいものを、いつも山奥へ遊びに出おって。本当に手を出されたとて、自業自得というものじゃ
column3: Ho ho, I'm the one who sent him to fetch the phoenix egg. And you, girl, why won't you ever listen to your mother and stay put in the city living in comfort? Always running off to play deep in the mountains... If someone really did take liberties with you, it would serve you right.

column2: えへへ、お城はすっごく退屈なんだもん。山のほうが楽しいんだよ！
column3: Hee hee, the city's so boring. The mountains are way more fun!

column2: 李少侠、ついでに紹介しておこう。阿奴はわしの一番下の弟子でな…
column3: Young hero Li, let me introduce her while we're at it. Anu is my youngest disciple...

column2: この子はほかに悪い癖はないのじゃが、少々遊び好きで、人にべったりくっつきたがる。一緒におるなら、気をつけることじゃな。ほっほっほ…！
column3: The girl has no other faults, only that she's a bit too fond of play, and clingy besides. You'd best be careful around her. Ho ho ho...!

column2: 彼女は…先輩の愛弟子だったんですか。道理で、あの若さであれほどの腕前なわけだ！
column3: She... so she's your prized disciple, Elder. No wonder she's so skilled at such a young age!

column2: お前たち、まだ用事が残っておるのじゃろう。早く済ませておいで
column3: You two still have business to finish. Off you go and see to it.

column2: おばあちゃん、阿奴、また今度会いに来るね
column3: Granny, Anu will come see you again another day.

column2: ほっほっ、さあ行っておいで！
column3: Ho ho, go on now!

column2: こ…ここはどこなんだ？　君の欲しいものは、ここにあるのか？
column3: Wh-what is this place? The thing you're after is in here?

column2: そうだよ。昨日一度忍び込んで、ここにあるのは確かめたんだ。でも、あいつらの親玉が強すぎて、あたしじゃかなわなくて。だけど今日は、その魔物の親玉が出かけるのを見たの。洞窟に残ってるのは小妖怪だけだし、あんたも加勢してくれるんだから、今度こそ絶対うまくいくよ！
column3: That's right. I sneaked in once yesterday and made sure it's in here. Too bad their boss is too strong, I couldn't beat him. But today I saw that fiend go out. Only some small fry are left in the cave, and with you backing me up, this time we can't fail!

column2: なんだよ、結局…俺を用心棒にしようってことか？
column3: So after all that... you brought me along as hired muscle?

column2: えへへ、聖獣の金翅鳳凰を倒せる人なら、ここの小妖怪なんかに腕で負けるはずないもんね
column3: Hee hee. Anyone who can beat the sacred Golden-Winged Phoenix surely won't lose to the small fry in here.

column2: ちぇっ、まんまと乗せられた…
column3: Tch... I've been roped right in...

column2: くやしい…空っぽだ！　昨日は確かに、あいつがここに入れるのを見たのに
column3: Damn... it's empty! I clearly saw him put it in here yesterday.

column2: 君はいったい何を探してるんだ？
column3: What exactly are you looking for?

column2: 教えてあげてもいいか…あたしはね、水霊珠を探してるんだよ！
column3: No harm in telling you... I'm looking for the Water Orb!

column2: 霊珠？　雷霊珠と風霊珠なら持ってるけど、代わりになるか？
column3: An orb? I've got the Thunder Orb and the Wind Orb here. Would they do instead?

column2: 本当に分かってないの？　それとも、あたしをからかってるの？
column3: Do you really not know, or are you making fun of me?

column2: 俺が知ってるのは、この霊珠は妖怪が術の修行に使う宝物らしい、ってことくらいで…
column3: All I know is that these orbs seem to be treasures demons use to cultivate their magic...

column2: なにが妖怪だよ！　知らないくせに、いいかげんなこと言わないで
column3: Demons, my foot! Don't talk nonsense about things you don't know.

column2: あたしたち苗族の言い伝えではね、大昔、北の蛮族とあたしたち南の苗族が戦になったの。はじめは蛮族があたしたちに負けた。そこで蛮族の法師が術を使って、天の神様に助けを求めたんだ。天帝は水、火、雷、風の四神と、魔女の旱魃を下界に遣わして、あたしたち苗族を攻めさせた。ところが戦が終わっても、五柱の神魔は天に帰ろうとしなかった。そのせいで、天の雷と地の火が地上の草木を焼き尽くし、日照りと飢饉で家畜が群れごと飢え死にして、そのうえ洪水が大地をすっかり呑み込んで、苗族も蛮族も住む土地を失ってしまったの。その時、人の姿に蛇の体を持つ巫女が現れて、四神を討ち、旱魃を封印し、洪水を鎮めて、大地に命を取り戻してくれた。その巫女こそ、あたしたち一族があがめる女媧様なんだよ
column3: According to the legends of us Miao, in ancient times the barbarian tribes of the north went to war with us Miao of the south. At first the barbarians were beaten. So their sorcerers worked a rite and begged their gods in heaven for help, and the Heavenly Emperor sent the four gods of Water, Fire, Thunder and Wind, along with the demoness Hanba, down to earth to fight us Miao. But when the war was over, the five gods and demons refused to return to heaven. Lightning from the sky and fire from the earth burned away every plant and tree, drought and famine starved the herds to death, and then a flood swallowed the whole land. Miao and barbarian alike lost their homes. Then a sorceress with a human form and a serpent's body appeared. She slew the four gods, sealed away Hanba, quelled the flood and brought the land back to life. That sorceress is Lady Nuwa, whom our people worship.

column2: 女媧様は、暴れた五柱の神魔の亡骸を練り上げて五つの霊珠に変え、後の世に伝えたの。代々それを使って、数えきれない苗族の民を守るようにって…。でも、巫后様の代になって、ある異変が起きて、五つの霊珠はあちこちに散らばり、妖怪たちに拾われて自分のものにされちゃったんだよ
column3: Lady Nuwa refined the bones of the five rampaging gods and demons into five orbs and handed them down to later generations, so that her successors could use them, age after age, to protect the countless Miao people... But in the Witch Queen's generation, something went wrong. The five orbs were scattered far and wide, and demons picked them up and kept them for themselves.

column2: そんな由来があったのか…
column3: So there's a whole story behind them...

column2: あたしが調べたところじゃ、水霊珠はここの妖怪が持ってるんだよ
column3: From what I've tracked down, the Water Orb is in the hands of the demons here.

column2: もし本当だとしても、わざわざ妖怪と奪い合うことはないだろ。危険すぎる！
column3: Even if that's true, it's not worth fighting demons over it. It's too risky!

column2: あたしが遊びで探してるとでも思ってるの！？　あたしたちの苗疆はひどい日照りで、もうずっとずっと雨が降ってないんだよ。川の水は干上がって、食べ物ももうすぐ尽きちゃう…。白苗と黒苗は水源を奪い合って、もう九年も戦を続けてるんだから！
column3: You think I'm doing this for fun!? Our Miao lands are suffering a terrible drought. It hasn't rained in ages, the rivers have run dry, and the food is almost gone... The White Miao and the Black Miao have been at war over water for nine years now!

column2: おかしな話だな。戦をして何が解決するんだ？
column3: That's odd. What does fighting a war solve?

column2: だからだよ。あたしは水霊珠を見つけなきゃいけないの
column3: Exactly. That's why I have to find the Water Orb.

column2: あたしの母さんが若い頃にも、一度ひどい日照りがあったんだって。その頃まだ女祭司だった巫后様が、水霊珠で術を使って天を祭ったら、日照りは収まったの。だからあたしは信じてる。水霊珠さえ見つかれば、何もかも解決するって
column3: When my mother was young there was a great drought too. The Witch Queen was only a priestess back then, and she used the Water Orb in a rite to Heaven, and the drought ended. So I believe that if we just find the Water Orb, all of this can be solved.

column2: へえ、その若さでそんな志を持ってるとは、見かけによらないな…。よし、手伝おう
column3: Heh. I wouldn't have guessed someone so young had such resolve... All right, I'll help you.

column2: 思うに、水霊珠は洞窟の外へ持ち出されたのかもしれない。外の近くを探してみよう。何か見つかるかもしれないぞ
column3: My guess is the Water Orb's been taken out of the cave. Let's search around outside. We might turn something up.

column2: ちょっと待って！　まずはここのお宝を全部いただいてからだよ
column3: Wait a moment! First let's take all the treasure here.

column2: 無駄足にはできないもん。どうせ全部、妖怪がかき集めてきたものなんだし、もらわなきゃ損だよ！)
column3: We can't have come all this way for nothing. The demons looted all of this anyway, so it'd be a waste not to take it!)

column2: そこのおばさん、ちょっとお尋ねしますが…
column3: Excuse me, ma'am, may I ask...

column2: きゃ～あ！！
column3: Eeeeek!!

column2: あんた誰？　入ってこないで！
column3: Who are you? Don't come in!

column2: あなたたち、だあれ？
column3: Who are you people?

column2: 丹丹！　早く中へ入りなさい！
column3: Dandan! Get inside, quick!

column2: どうして…ここの人たちは、俺たちを見たとたん隠れちまうんだ？
column3: Why... does everyone here hide the moment they see us?

column2: あっ…！
あの、あなた方は…？
column3: Excuse me, you are...?

column2: よかった、やっと話をしてくれる人がいた
column3: Thank goodness, at last someone willing to talk to us.

column2: どうやってここへ入ってきたのですか？　普通、よその人にこの村が見つかるはずはないのですが
column3: How did you get in here? Outsiders normally can't possibly find our village.

column2: 俺たち、わけも分からないうちにここへ来ちまったんだ
column3: We just sort of wandered in here without knowing how.

column2: そうだ…ここはどういう所なんだい？　どうして村の人たちは、俺たちを見ると隠れてしまうんだ
column3: By the way... what is this place? Why do the villagers hide when they see us?

column2: ここは桃源村といいます。よその人が村に入ってくることは、めったにありません
column3: This place is called Peach Spring Village. Outsiders very rarely find their way in.

column2: それに最近、ある出来事がありまして。それで皆、知らない人を見ると怖がるのです
column3: And something happened recently, so everyone is afraid when they see strangers.

column2: 阿桃や、もう懲りたのを忘れたのかい？　よそ者をむやみに信じちゃいけないよ！
column3: Atao, have you forgotten your lesson already? Don't go trusting outsiders so easily!

column2: そうだよ、阿桃…。外の人間なんて、ろくなもんじゃないんだから。また騙されちゃだめだよ
column3: That's right, Atao... People from outside are all no good. Don't get fooled a second time.

column2: わしらの桃源郷は昔から世間と隔たり、自給自足で、何の憂いもなく暮らしてきたんだ。それがあの宋賀文とかいう若造が来てからというもの、何もかも変わっちまった
column3: Our Peach Spring has always been cut off from the world, self-sufficient and free of care. Ever since that boy Song Hewen came, everything has changed.

column2: そうだよ！　あの若造はとんでもないやつさ。あんなに良くしてやったのに、恩を仇で返すなんて
column3: That's right! That boy is a real scoundrel. After all our kindness to him, he repaid it with betrayal.

column2: 皆さん、誤解しないでください。俺たちは悪人じゃありません。ここへ来たのに悪気は何もないんです
column3: Please don't misunderstand, everyone. We're not bad people. We mean no harm in coming here.

column2: あんたのことじゃないよ。あたしらが言ってるのは、あの宋って名のろくでなしのことさ
column3: I wasn't talking about you. We mean that bastard Song.

column2: 教えてもらえませんか。その宋なんとかってやつは、いったい何をしたんです？　皆さんがそこまで憎むなんて
column3: Could you tell me what this Song whoever-he-is actually did to make you hate him so much?

column2: だめだ。桃源郷の秘密は、絶対によそ者に知られてはならん。さもないと大変なことになる
column3: No. The secret of Peach Spring must never be known to outsiders, or there will be big trouble.

column2: 今さらそんなこと言って何になる？　阿桃の親父さんは、もうやつらに連れていかれちまったんだぞ
column3: What's the use of saying that now? Atao's father has already been taken by them.

column2: かわいそうに。村長はあの歳だ、悪党どもの責め苦に耐えられるはずがない。もう宝の隠し場所を白状させられたかもしれん
column3: The poor man. At his age the village elder can't possibly withstand what those villains will put him through. He may already have given up where the treasure is hidden.

column2: はあ…。ひと月前、阿桃が、桃の林に迷い込んだ薬草採りの医者を助けて、桃花の瘴気の毒まで治してやったんだ。よそ者がここへ来るのは珍しいことだから、わしらも主人としてもてなそうと、何日か泊めて歓待した。そして最後は習わしどおり、桃源郷から送り出す前に仙水を飲ませて、ここでのことをすべて忘れさせるはずだった。ところが、なんと阿桃がその仙水をこっそりすり替えていたんだ
column3: Sigh... A month ago, Atao rescued a herb-gathering physician who had strayed into the peach forest, and even cured his peach-blossom miasma. Since outsiders so rarely come here, we wanted to do our duty as hosts, so we put him up for a few days. In the end, as is our custom, before seeing him out of Peach Spring we had him drink the immortal water so that he would forget everything about this place. Who could have known that Atao had secretly switched the water?

column2: あの野郎は実に欲深い。桃源郷に宝があると知ると、妖しい道士どもと手を組んで奪いに来やがった。やつらは村長をさらって、宝のありかを吐かせようとしているんだ
column3: That wretch is so greedy. Once he learned our Peach Spring had a treasure, he plotted with a band of evil Taoists to come and seize it. They carried off the village elder to force the treasure's whereabouts out of him.

column2: そうだ、あんたら、まさかやつらの仲間じゃないだろうな？
column3: Say, you wouldn't happen to be in league with them too, would you?

column2: いやいや、俺が何より憎んでるのも、恩知らずな連中なんだ。そいつらがどこにいるか教えてくれ。村長を助け出してやるよ
column3: No, no. There's nothing I hate more than ungrateful scum myself. Tell me where those fellows are, and I'll rescue your elder for you.

column2: 本当ですか！　よかった…
column3: Really! Oh, thank goodness...

column2: 阿桃！　またやってる。そんなに簡単によそ者を信じて
column3: Atao! There you go again, trusting outsiders so easily.

column2: でも…お父さんが心配で…
column3: But... I'm so worried about Father...

column2: あの鼻の長い道士が言ってたじゃないか。宝さえ差し出せば、村長に手出しはしないって
column3: Didn't that long-nosed Taoist say that as long as the treasure is handed over, they won't harm the elder?

column2: でも…お父さんがあの人たちと行ってから、もう半日以上になるわ。もしかして…
column3: But... Father has been gone with them most of the day already. What if...

column2: あんたたちの言ってるその鼻の長い道士って、木道人って名前じゃない？
column3: That long-nosed Taoist you're talking about, is he called Taoist Mu?

column2: どうして知ってるんだ？
column3: How do you know that?

column2: あはっ、やっぱり！　あの木道人は木の精が化けたやつでね、あちこちで珍しいお宝を集めるのが大好きで、手に入らなきゃ力ずくで奪うんだよ。あたしたちもちょうどあいつを探してて、取り返したいものがあるの。ねえ、あいつがどこにいるか早く教えて！
column3: Ha! That settles it! That Taoist Mu is a tree spirit in disguise. He loves collecting rare treasures from all over, and what he can't get, he takes by force. We happen to be looking for him too, to get something back. Quick, tell me where he is!

column2: 父はあの人たちを連れて、こちらの方角から林の中へ入っていきました
column3: My father led them into the forest in this direction.

column2: どうか父を助け出してください。それから…宋様を、ひどい目に遭わせないでください
column3: Please, bring my father back safe. And... please don't be hard on Young Master Song.

column2: 宋様は…根は悪い人ではありません。こんなことをしたのは、きっと無理強いされたからです
column3: Young Master Song... he isn't bad at heart. He must have been forced into doing this.

column2: でもねえ、あんたたち、あの妖しい道士どもに勝てるだけの腕があるのかい？
column3: But do you really have what it takes to beat that band of evil Taoists?

column2: やつらは妖術を使うんだよ！　むざむざ死にに行くことはないよ
column3: They use sorcery! Don't go throwing your lives away for nothing.

column2: はじめに見た時は、宋賀文は悪人には見えなかったんだけどねえ？
column3: From the look of Song Hewen at first, he didn't seem like a villain, did he?

column2: ああ…村長が連れていかれるのを目の前で見ていながら、わしらは何ひとつ手を打てなかった。
column3: Sigh... We watched the elder being dragged off right before our eyes, and there was nothing any of us could do.

column2: だからよそ者は信じちゃならんと言ったんだ。これはご先祖代々の教えだぞ。やはり年寄りの言うことを聞かんと、たちまち痛い目を見る！
column3: I knew outsiders couldn't be trusted. That's the teaching our ancestors handed down through the generations. Sure enough, ignore your elders' words and you pay for it soon enough!

column2: 報いだ、報いだよ！
column3: Retribution, this is retribution!

column2: ああ、人は見かけによらんものだなあ
column3: Ah, you can know a man's face but not his heart.

column2: えっ！？　あなた方は…
column3: Huh!? You are...

column2: あんたが宋の若様だな？
column3: You must be Young Master Song?

column2: はい…私は宋賀文と申します。貴殿、何かご指導でも？
column3: Yes... I am Song Hewen. What can I do for you, sir?

column2: 指導？　ぶん殴ってやりたい気分だよ！
column3: Do for me? I feel like punching someone!

column2: あ…あなた方、何をするつもりですか！？
column3: Wh-what do you want with me!?

column2: 聞くが…あんた、桃源村の人たちに恩を仇で返したうえ、妖しい道士どもを連れてきて宝を奪おうとしたんだろう
column3: Let me ask you... did you repay the people of Peach Spring Village with betrayal, and bring a band of evil Taoists here to seize their treasure?

column2: わ…私も、こんなことになるとは思わなかったんです。はじめ、彼らが力を貸してくれると言ったので、それで…
column3: I... I never thought it would come to this. At first they said they could help me, so...

column2: それで、宝を見て欲が出たってわけか？
column3: So the sight of treasure gave you ideas?

column2: 違います！　寿葫蘆のためではありません。その…その…阿桃さんのためなんです
column3: No! It wasn't for the Life Gourd. It was... it was... for Miss Atao.

column2: へえ？　話が見えなくなってきたぞ。正直に白状しろ。さもないと痛い目を見るぜ！
column3: Oh? Now you've lost me. Come clean with me, or you'll be sorry!

column2: あの時、私は桃花の林で道に迷い、瘴毒にもあたってしまいました。幸い阿桃さんが助けてくれたのです。その後…村の人たちが私を送り出そうという時、阿桃さんはこっそり仙水をすり替えました。それは…私に、自分のことを忘れてほしくなかったからです
column3: I had lost my way in the peach-blossom forest and been poisoned by the miasma. Luckily, Atao saved me. Later... when they were about to send me away, Atao secretly switched the immortal water. Because... she didn't want me to forget her.

column2: はははっ、そういうことだったのか。本当に、連中の宝が目当てじゃないんだな？
column3: Ha ha ha! So that's what happened. You're really not after their treasure?

column2: はい、私はただ阿桃さんと一緒にいたいだけなのです。ですが村の人たちは、よそ者が桃源村に留まることを断じて許しません。それで私は記憶を頼りに道をたどってひそかに戻り、阿桃さんを連れ出そうと考えました。でも…村人に見つかるのが怖くて。そんな時、桃花の林の外で木道人に出会ったのです。力を貸してやると言うので、彼らを連れて桃花の林を抜け、ここへ入りました。ところが…彼らは私を利用していただけで…。私には鶏一羽つかまえる力もなく、彼にはかないません。村の人たちにもひどく誤解されて、私は…私はもう、どうしたらいいのか分からないのです
column3: Yes. All I want is to be with Atao. But the villagers absolutely refuse to let an outsider stay in Peach Spring Village. So I retraced the way from memory and slipped back, hoping to take Atao away with me. But... I was afraid the villagers would catch me. Then I met Taoist Mu outside the peach-blossom forest. He said he could help me, so I led them through the forest and in here. Who knew... they were only using me... I haven't the strength to truss a chicken, so I'm no match for him, and the villagers have completely misjudged me. I... I truly don't know what to do.

column2: 分かった、あんたは脇へどいてな。その木道人とやらには、俺が会ってやる！
column3: All right, step aside. I'll go have a word with this Taoist Mu!

column2: 彼の手にある金の鈴には、くれぐれもお気をつけください。木道人は金の鈴を使って、とても恐ろしい術を繰り出すのです
column3: Be very careful of the golden bell in his hand. Taoist Mu uses it to cast some very powerful magic.

column2: ほっほ、もうじき、もうじき着きますわい…
column3: Ho ho... soon, we're nearly there...

column3: You've told me that sixty-eight times already! If you don't take me to the Life Gourd right now, I'll butcher you!

column2: やれやれ…のう、道長どの。あんたほどの修行があれば、おとなしく分をわきまえておるだけで、数百年生きるのも難しくはなかろうに。なにゆえ寿葫蘆などに頼るのかね？
column3: Sigh... Now, Reverend Taoist, with your level of cultivation, if you just kept to yourself, living a few hundred years shouldn't be hard. Why rely on the Life Gourd?

column2: 黙れ！　そんな宝があると知ったからには、是が非でも手に入れてやるわ！
column3: Enough talk! Now that I know such a treasure exists, I must have it!

column3: Obtained Astral Orb

column3: Father... I made you suffer. This whole disaster was my doing.

column2: お前のせいではないよ。お前に悪気はなかったのじゃから。責めるなら、珍しい宝など持って人の欲を招いた、わしら自身を責めるべきじゃ
column3: You're not to blame; you meant no harm. If anything is to blame, it's that we kept a treasure that drew covetous eyes.

column2: 幸い、お二人の英雄が義によって助けてくださり、この村は災難を免れることができました

column2: ははは、大したことじゃないさ！　気にしないでくれ
column3: Ha ha, it was nothing! Please don't give it another thought.

column2: そうそう。また恩返ししたいって女の子が出てきたら、この人、身がもたないもんね！
column3: That's right. If yet another girl wanted to repay him, he'd never be able to handle it!

column3: Young man, come here!

column2: はい…
column3: Yes...

column3: Father, I brought all of this about. Please don't blame Young Master Song. If you must punish someone, punish me.

column3: What are you so worked up about? I never said I was going to do anything to him.

column2: 阿桃さん…もう私のためにとりなしてくださらなくていいのです。そうされると、私はなおさら良心が痛みます…

column3: No... if it hadn't been for me...

column2: 二人して何を言い争っておるのじゃ？　誰かを責めるなどとは言っておらんぞ！
column3: What are you two arguing about? I never said I was blaming anyone!

column2: 悪いのはこのわしの老いぼれた目じゃ。娘がよその者を好きになったことに気づきもせなんだ。それでこんな騒ぎになってしもうた！
column3: The fault lies with my dim old eyes. I never noticed that my daughter had fallen for an outsider, and that is what caused all this trouble!

column2: お父さん…
column3: Father...

column3: Young man, do you truly love Atao?

column3: Yes... I beg your blessing, sir.

column3: I know...

column3: Good... Come here, and eat this peach.

column3: Whoa...

column3: What's the Water Orb supposed to look like?

column3: My mother says it's a water-blue jewel about the size of a thumb. Moisture seeps from its surface all by itself, and when you get close to it you feel a chill.

column3: Heh... the way you describe it, it sounds like the marbles I used to play with as a kid.

column2: でたらめ言わないでよ！
column3: Oh, stop talking rubbish!

column2: それで、君の鳳凰の卵は、いつになったらくれるんだ？
column3: So when do I get that phoenix egg of yours?

column2: 何を焦ってるの？　あげないなんて言ってないでしょ。鳳凰のヒナがかえったら、残った殻はちゃんとあんたのものだよ！　それとも、この小さな命を傷つけても平気なの？
column3: What's the rush? It's not like I won't give it to you. Once the baby phoenix hatches, the leftover shell is all yours! Or could you really bear to hurt this little life?

column2: 分かったよ、待てばいいんだろ
column3: All right, all right, I'll wait.

column3: Then... in the meantime, I'll take you to get the "Fire Qilin Horn" first.

column2: 麒麟の角！　どこにあるか知ってるのか？
column3: The qilin horn! You know where it is?

column2: 知らないわけないでしょ。でもね、まず母さんの許しをもらわなきゃだめなんだよ
column3: Of course I know. But first we need my mother's permission.

column2: 君のお袋さん？
column3: Your mother?

column2: もう、いいからついてきてよ
column3: Oh, just come with me, all right?

column3: A thick fog fills the forest. You cannot go on.

column2: 阿奴が風霊珠を掲げると、たちまち一陣の風が濃い霧を吹き払った
column3: Anu raises the Wind Orb, and at once a gust of wind blows the thick fog away.

column2: お三方、万事めでたく収まって何よりです。俺たちもそろそろ失礼します…
column3: Congratulations to the three of you on a happy ending. We should be on our way too...

column2: お待ちくだされ。この年寄りから、お二人の英雄に差し上げたいものがありましてな
column3: Wait. This old man has something he would like to give you two heroes.

column3: Ooh! What kind of treasure?)

column3: If the lady hero will look inside the well on her left, she will see...

column3: Wow, look! It's a gourd carved out of amber!

column3: Sir, this is far too valuable. We can't accept it.

column2: ちょっと！　あんたって頭が固いんだから。せっかく心からくれるって言ってるんだよ。あんたがいらなくても、あたしはいらないなんて言ってないからね
column3: Hey! You're so stubborn. He's offering it to us in all sincerity. You may not want it, but I never said I didn't!

column2: ほっほっ、これは寿葫蘆といいましてな、わしが若い頃、ふとした折に手に入れた世にも稀な宝ですじゃ
column3: Ho ho. This is the Life Gourd, a rare treasure I came upon by chance when I was young.

column2: じゃが、これはわしら桃源村の者には何の役にも立たぬうえ、このような騒ぎまで招いてしもうた
column3: But to us folk of Peach Spring Village it is of no use at all, and it has brought this trouble down on us besides.

column2: それならお二人に差し上げたほうがよい。江湖を渡り歩くあなた方には、多少なりとも役に立ちましょう
column3: Better to give it to you two. For those who roam the martial world, it should be of some help.

column2: では、お言葉に甘えて、ありがたく頂戴します
column3: Then I shall respectfully do as you say and accept.

column2: ほっほっ、会うは別れの始めと申します。この年寄りに、途中までお見送りさせてくだされ…
column3: Ho ho. All good things must come to an end. Let this old man see you on your way...

column2: まさか、あたしたちにも仙水を飲ませて、ここのことを忘れさせるつもりじゃないよね？
column3: You're not going to make us drink the immortal water and forget this place too, are you?

column2: お二人はわしらの恩人。どうしてそのような真似ができましょうか
column3: You two are our benefactors. How could we treat you so?

column2: お二人がまたこの地を通ることがあって、この桃の木々にたわわに実がなっているのを見かけたら、わしの孫の満一か月の祝い酒を飲みに来るのを忘れんでくだされよ。ほっほっ…
column3: If you two ever pass this way again and see these peach trees heavy with fruit, don't forget to come drink to my grandchild's first month. Ho ho...

column2: あんたたち、桃の木の精だったのか！　じゃあ…宋さんは…
column3: So you're peach tree spirits! Then... Brother Song...

column3: Thank you... Farewell.

column3: This girl has been gathering all the true qi in her body to shield the child in her womb. As long as that qi holds, and with my elixirs besides, she'll be fine for ten days or half a month.

column3: Don't rejoice too soon. Whether her body can recover is still very much in doubt...

column3: To heal the wounds of mother and child, you must obtain two things: the "Phoenix Egg" and the "Qilin Horn".

column2: この霊山の"神木林"の奥で"金翅鳳凰"の巣を見つければ、その卵の殻が取れる。白苗族の住む"大理城の麒麟洞"には、千年を経た火眼麒麟の精がおってな、これを降せば角が手に入る。じゃが、よく覚えておくのじゃ…この二頭は我ら苗族の聖獣。薬を取るだけにして、命を奪ってはならん。さもなくば天罰が下るぞ
column3: Deep in the "Sacred Wood" here on Spirit Mountain, find the nest of the "Golden-Winged Phoenix" and you can take its eggshell. In the "Qilin Cave of Dali", where the White Miao live, there is a thousand-year-old fire-eyed qilin spirit. Subdue it and you can take its horn. But remember... these two beasts are sacred to us Miao. Take only the medicine and do not harm their lives, or Heaven will punish you.

column3: By the way... where's Yueru? I'll ask Yueru to come with me. She's sharper than I am; with her along we're less likely to slip up.

column3: The young couple's lives have been saved. But as for Miss Lin, there was nothing I could do.

column3: Sigh... All the world knows your healing arts are without equal. Can even you not bring that girl back?

column3: Bringing her back to life is impossible. But ways to keep her from dying... those I have plenty of.

column3: I'm afraid your words have me confused.

column3: Ho ho... when the time comes, you'll understand. Only, I can't promise it will succeed.

column3: Very well. Whatever happens, please do help these children...

column3: Your wounds are nearly healed. You can go out and walk about now. Granny here will keep watch over the two girls for you.

column3: Remember this well: the Golden-Winged Phoenix likes to nest at the tops of giant trees. Search the high places of the Sacred Wood and you may find something.

column3: Around the outskirts of Dali, the Black Miao and White Miao are often at war. I suggest you stay away for now, and go to the Fire Qilin Cave once things have calmed down.
